nodes.detailed_figure_description: A cylindrical wire is drawn horizontally. Its left circular cross-section is labeled A. A right-pointing arrow above the wire is labeled I, indicating conventional current. A right-pointing blue arrow inside is labeled E, indicating the electric field. A short section of the wire is marked dx. To the right, a squiggly electron path and an e-minus symbol illustrate random electron motion. The accompanying note says, “e⁻ travel randomly but with average ‘drift’ opposing current.”
nodes.figure_alternative: Wire diagram showing current and electric field to the right, while electrons move randomly with an average drift opposite the current.

nodes.spoken_math_alternative: I equals e times n times A times v sub d, where e is elementary charge, n is the number of electrons per volume, A is cross-sectional area, and v sub d is drift velocity.
